summary: Michael Zimmermann works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Hamburg (~1993–2000) and studied at Soka University. He held posts at Nepal Research Centre (2002), Stanford (2003), and Hamburg (~2007).

Michael von Brück is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Rostock (1968–1973) and the University of Madras (~1980–1985), later holding professorships at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (~1991–2014).

Michaela Haas works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Bonn (attested 2008) under Peter Schwieger, and also studied under Rechungpa and Jigme Namgyal Dzigar Kongtrul.

Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Komazawa University and earned her Ph.D. at the University of Munich (–2014). She held posts at the University of Göttingen, UC Berkeley, and Stanford University (2016).

Michaël Peyrot specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (1999–2010), later holding posts at Leiden University (~2013, 2016) and the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2014–2016).

Michel Angot was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied under Marie-Claude Porcher at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1985–1991) and held appointments at Paris Nanterre University (~1992–2000), INALCO (~1994–2003), and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~2000–2024).

Michel Bitbol specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Paris Diderot University (~1980–1985) under Pierre Mills. His career includes posts at the CNRS (~1990, emeritus 2020), IHPST (~1997–2009), and École Normale Supérieure (~2014).

Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1852–1855) and in Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp (1857–1860). He held posts at the EPHE (1868–1882) and Collège de France (1864–1905).

Michel Clasquin-Johnson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral studies at the University of South Africa between ~1988 and ~1999, and held a post there beginning in 1990.

Michel Hulin was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1956) and under Olivier Lacombe at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1968–1977), where he subsequently served on the faculty from 1981 to 1998 (emeritus ~2003).
Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Boisselier (1988) and served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University from ~1989 to 2008.

Michel Ledrus was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held posts at KU Leuven (1931), the Pontifical Gregorian University (1932–1933), and served as spiritual director at Collegio Bellarmino (1949).

Michel Lejeune was a linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1926–1929) under Antoine Meillet (~1926–1931). He held positions at the University of Poitiers (~1937–1946), the University of Paris (~1951–1977), and the EPHE (~1951–1977).

Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Geneva, studying under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Geneva (1987–1992), Hanazono University (attested 2000–2006), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (2007).

Michel Soymié was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at INALCO (-1952) and held posts at the CNRS (1951–1956), EFEO (~1952–1966), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1966–1992).

Michel Strickmann was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Leiden, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University, and held positions at UC Berkeley (1978), the University of Bordeaux (~1980–1981), and Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (1983–1985).

Michela Clemente is a Tibetologist who studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and conducted postdoctoral work under Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015). She held a post as a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

Michele Kerbaker was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin (~1853–1857) under Gaspare Gorresio and Giovanni Flechia. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1870) and University of Naples Federico II (~1872–1910).
Michele Martin works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and held a post at National Taiwan University.
Michelle Spuler is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Queensland and taught at Colorado College and Victoria University of Wellington.
